findings.title: VAL-05 real-provider and device proof remains an overall-close blocker
findings.rationale: DOD-05 and VAL-05 require actual Meta authorization, real QR/device pairing, and real IN/OUT plus recovery per modality. The packet and handoff explicitly record that no real Meta authorization, pairing, or real IN/OUT occurred; current runtime evidence is limited to configuration booleans and synthetic provider/header/ingress probes. The passing local suite establishes local behavior and harness fidelity, not this external boundary. This does not invalidate local implementation readiness, but it blocks overall TODO closure.
findings.suggested_action: Keep the TODO active and execute the approved external VAL-05 matrix when authorized test targets are available: Embedded Signup and selected official resource, QR/device pairing and identity verification, authenticated IN to the correct BU/inbox, actual OUT received by the interlocutor, and permitted recovery for each modality. Record redacted build/target/time outcomes; do not substitute provider doubles or repeat audits merely to restate this known gap.

findings.title: Fail-first provenance is incomplete despite effective final regression coverage
findings.rationale: The delivery history correctly identifies the cp18 fail-first log as a Compose preflight failure and the cp20 former-guard exercise as reconstructed test-after evidence. Browser FRC did expose a genuine defect, and the final tests are substantive rather than pass-the-test assertions, but no authentic pre-fix RED covers every behavior-defining contract. This is verification-process debt, not evidence that the current local behavior lacks regression protection.
findings.suggested_action: Classify the slice as mixed/test-after in closeout and do not fabricate historical RED evidence. For a future behavior-defining change or defect correction, capture a failing product-level test before the fix or record an explicit not-applicable rationale; retain the present barriers and negative controls as final regression protection.
